rationale: As Ricoh manufactures wide-format printers targeting the signage, vehicle wrap, and graphics markets, the VP of Product Development owns the product roadmap and strategic partnerships that enhance their printers' value proposition. Tedlar represents a critical opportunity for product differentiation - by partnering with or recommending Tedlar overlaminates, they can position their Pro L5160e and Pro TF6251 printers as complete solutions for customers demanding 12-20+ year outdoor durability. This role cares about competitive positioning against HP, Canon, and Epson in the large-format space, and being able to offer/recommend proven protective film solutions directly addresses customer pain points around UV degradation and warranty claims. Their KPIs include product portfolio performance, customer satisfaction scores, and market share growth in premium segments - all enhanced by associating Ricoh printers with industry-leading protective films. Given Ricoh's presence at PRINTING United and focus on serving 85% of Fortune 500 companies, this role would see Tedlar as a strategic enabler for premium market positioning and customer success.

The Director of Sales for Ricoh's wide-format printing division directly owns revenue targets and customer relationships with PSPs, sign manufacturers, and vehicle wrap installers - the exact companies that purchase Tedlar overlaminates. This role is measured on equipment sales, customer acquisition, and account expansion. By incorporating Tedlar into their sales conversations and potentially offering bundled solutions or qualified referrals, they can differentiate Ricoh printers on total cost of ownership and output durability rather than just print quality specs. When selling a $100K+ Pro L5160e printer, being able to recommend Tedlar as the protective film that ensures their customers' printed graphics last 12-20+ years outdoors creates a compelling value story that justifies premium pricing. This role personally benefits from reduced customer churn (fewer complaints about print durability), higher close rates in competitive deals, and expansion opportunities with existing accounts. Given Ricoh serves 1.4M businesses including Fortune 500 companies, this role would see Tedlar partnership as a competitive weapon and customer retention tool.

The Director of Business Development owns strategic partnerships, channel development, and new market opportunities for Ricoh's graphics and signage portfolio. This role is tasked with identifying adjacent revenue streams and ecosystem partnerships that enhance Ricoh's market position without requiring heavy R&D investment. A partnership with DuPont Tedlar represents a high-value, low-risk opportunity: co-marketing at trade shows like PRINTING United, creating joint customer success stories, developing certification programs that position Ricoh+Tedlar as the premium solution for outdoor durability, and potentially establishing referral revenue streams. Their KPIs include partnership revenue, new market penetration, and strategic relationship value. Given Ricoh already provides Sign & Graphics Professional Services including training programs, integrating Tedlar education and recommendations into their service offerings creates immediate value. This role would see Tedlar as a strategic asset that strengthens customer relationships, opens doors to architectural and transit markets where extreme durability matters, and differentiates Ricoh's commercial printing ecosystem from competitors who only sell equipment.
